question: What does a high-risk labour mean for a pregnant woman?

options.A: Routine childbirth requiring routine midwifery observations only
options.B: Any delivery lasting longer than two hours in the second stage
options.C: Increased danger to the life or health of mother or baby
options.D: Labour that exclusively occurs in tertiary healthcare institutions

explanation: High-risk labour carries an elevated probability of adverse outcomes for either the mother or the fetus compared to an uncomplicated birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h1)

question: Why is early identification of high-risk labour important in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It guarantees that every baby will be born vaginally
options.B: It eliminates the need to document fluid intake and output
options.C: It ensures that doctors do all the work instead of nurses
options.D: It prevents maternal mortality and severe complications like fistula

explanation: Spotting risks early allows the healthcare team to intervene before life-threatening emergencies or debilitating morbidities develop. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h1)

question: What is the main danger of severe pre-eclampsia during labour?

options.A: Rapid dilation of the cervix within thirty minutes
options.B: Premature closure of the anterior fontanelle in the neonate
options.C: Excessive production of amniotic fluid in the second stage
options.D: Reduced placental blood flow leading to fetal hypoxia

explanation: Vasospasm caused by high blood pressure restricts blood supply through the placenta, threatening the oxygen supply to the fetus. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h2)

question: A woman who has given birth many times (grand multipara) is most at risk for which complication during labour?

options.A: Postpartum hemorrhage due to uterine atony
options.B: Immediate shoulder dystocia from fetal macrosomia
options.C: Severe hypertension caused by renal failure
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes from polyhydramnios

explanation: Overstretched uterine muscles in women with many previous deliveries often fail to contract effectively after birth, leading to severe bleeding. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h2)

question: What does thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid during active labour usually mean?
explanation: Passing meconium in utero is often a sign that the fetus has experienced oxygen deprivation, causing anal sphincter relaxation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h3)

question: Why is a transverse fetal lie considered an emergency during labour?

options.A: The fetus will automatically turn head-down within one hour
options.B: Vaginal delivery is mechanically impossible without rotation or surgery
options.C: It causes immediate maternal hypertension and severe headaches
options.D: Intravenous oxytocin infusion will rapidly correct the lie

explanation: A transverse lie means the baby is positioned sideways across the pelvis, blocking normal descent and requiring a caesarean section. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h3)

question: Which instrument is commonly used to listen to the fetal heart rate intermittently?
explanation: The Pinard stethoscope is a traditional acoustic device used widely across Nigerian maternity wards to listen to the fetal heartbeat. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of monitoring uterine contractions in high-risk labour?

options.A: To prevent uterine hyperstimulation and fetal oxygen deprivation
options.B: To measure the exact maternal blood glucose level
options.C: To determine the exact birth weight of the infant
options.D: To calculate the total volume of amniotic fluid lost

explanation: Excessive or overly frequent contractions restrict blood flow to the placenta, threatening fetal oxygenation during childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a partograph during labour?

options.A: To record the financial cost of hospital treatment for the patient
options.B: To serve as a legal prescription chart for intrapartum medications
options.C: To track the postnatal recovery of the mother after delivery
options.D: To provide a pictorial overview of labour progress and maternal-fetal wellbeing

explanation: The partograph is a standardized chart that helps midwives visualize labour progression and detect deviations early. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h5)

question: What should a nurse do when the cervical dilation curve crosses the action line on a partograph?

options.A: Escalate care and initiate urgent intervention or transfer
options.B: Discharge the patient home for observation over the weekend
options.C: Reduce the frequency of maternal blood pressure checks to hourly
options.D: Wait for another four hours before performing any further vaginal exam

explanation: Crossing the action line indicates that labour is abnormal, requiring immediate intervention such as augmentation or caesarean section. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h5)

question: Which maternal position helps improve blood flow to the placenta during a high-risk labour?
explanation: Lying on the left side relieves pressure from the gravid uterus on the inferior vena cava, enhancing cardiac output and placental perfusion. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h6)

question: A woman in labour shows signs of fetal distress. What immediate nursing action should be prioritized?

options.A: Ensure secure intravenous access and reposition to the left side
options.B: Instruct the patient to hold her breath and push vigorously
options.C: Encourage walking around the ward to speed up cervical dilation
options.D: Administer an enema to empty the lower bowel completely

explanation: Establishing IV access prepares the nurse for emergency drug administration, while lateral positioning instantly improves fetal oxygenation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h6)

question: What is the immediate priority nursing action when an umbilical cord prolapse occurs?

options.A: Manually elevate the presenting part off the umbilical cord
options.B: Perform a fundal pressure maneuver to hasten fetal expulsion
options.C: Apply warm compresses to the maternal perineal area
options.D: Administer oral analgesics and wait for spontaneous delivery

explanation: Lifting the baby's head away from the cord prevents fatal compression of blood vessels until emergency delivery can occur. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h7)

question: Why is magnesium sulfate given to a patient having eclamptic seizures during labour?

options.A: To increase the clotting factors in the bloodstream
options.B: To accelerate the dilation of the uterine cervix
options.C: To lower the maternal blood sugar level rapidly
options.D: To prevent and control recurrent convulsive seizures

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for managing and preventing eclampsia in high-risk obstetric patients. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of actively managing the third stage of labour?

options.B: To speed up the expulsion of the placenta
options.C: To reduce the duration of the first stage
options.D: To stimulate early breast milk production

explanation: Active management involves uterotonic administration, controlled cord traction, and uterine massage to minimize excessive bleeding after birth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h8)

question: Which assessment is most important during the first two hours after delivery for a high-risk mother?

options.A: Monitoring uterine tone and lochial blood loss
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the newborn's head
options.C: Checking visual acuity and pupillary light reflexes
options.D: Assessing the mother's ability to walk unassisted

explanation: Postpartum hemorrhage is a leading cause of maternal mortality, making frequent checks on uterine firmness and vaginal bleeding essential. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h8)
